verification.scope: Execution and contract checks; business ambiguities require operator answers

notes: Join direction: Master is the population (SKU x Company x Item code); Stock supplies /qty per Company + Item code. Items present only in Stock and absent from Master cannot receive a SKU and should not create new identities.

Item code is stored as a number in both sheets, so its zero padding is already lost at read time; matching must be done on zero-stripped numeric values or on the numeric suffix of the zero-padded SKU, never on raw string equality.
SKU prefix (TH-/MY-) appears to encode the same company as the Company column; this is consistent in the supplied values but is only a join sanity check, not an output field.
'Quantity pieces' is unambiguous about units and no VAT, currency or price fields exist in either sheet, so no business clarification is required for this contract.

tables.reason: Sheet 'Master' is a 12-row product master: one row per SKU (12 distinct SKU values, unique_ratio 1.0), with a company code, an item code that repeats once per company (6 codes x 2 companies) and a human description ('TH item 1', 'MY item 1', ...). No prices, quantities, promotions or category hierarchy, so it is the product/identity table and supplies the output identity /sku and /product_name.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Header is literally SKU; 12 distinct values out of 12 rows, sku_like hint, format '<COMPANY>-<4-digit code>' (TH-0001, MY-0003) with zero-padded numeric suffix. This is the unique output identity the operator names, and being text it preserves the leading zeros that the integer 'Item code' column loses.

columns.name: Company
columns.reason: Only two values, TH (6) and MY (6), matching the SKU prefix. It is a company/legal-entity code, not a product attribute, and the contract has no field for it; it must be kept as half of the cross-sheet join key because the operator states item codes are unique only within a company.

columns.name: Item code
columns.reason: 6 distinct values (1-6) repeated across the two companies; header 'Item code' and it equals the numeric part of SKU (TH-0001 -> 0001). It is the ERP item number scoped per company, used only to join to 'Stock'; it has no target pointer and its integer typing means leading zeros are already lost, so joining must compare zero-stripped values or use the SKU suffix.

columns.name: Description
columns.reason: 12 distinct free-text values, one per SKU ('TH item 1', 'MY item 4'), no nulls - the product description/label required by /product_name from the master list.

tables.reason: Sheet 'Stock' holds only Company, Item code and 'Quantity pieces' - a per-company stock on-hand snapshot with no identity or name of its own, so it is the inventory/quantity source for /qty. No single column is unique (Item code repeats once per company, quantity values are just measures), so the row key is the composite Company + Item code that matches Master; joining on Item code alone would double every quantity across companies.

columns.name: Company
columns.reason: Two values, MY (6) and TH (6), same code set as Master's Company; it is the company scope of the item code and part of the join key, not an output field in the contract.

columns.name: Item code
columns.reason: 6 distinct integers repeated across the two companies, header matches Master's 'Item code'. Used only to join to Master on Company + Item code; no target pointer exists for it and its int typing means it must be compared zero-stripped.

columns.name: Quantity pieces
columns.reason: Header explicitly states the unit ('pieces'), 12 distinct integers 11-166 with no nulls - stock in individual pieces, exactly the /qty semantic, so no unit conversion is needed. Values are integers, so precision is preserved without rounding; missing rows stay null rather than zero.

problems: compile: source column 'products.Quantity pieces' not found; values will be null

changes_from_draft: Added the second source 'stock' (sheet 'Stock') and a left join products←stock on Company + Item code with normalize_keys trim/upper/strip_leading_zeros, because item codes are unique only within a company (operator rule) and raw cells show zero-padded text in both sheets.

Fixed the /qty failure: 'Quantity pieces' exists only in the Stock sheet, so the expression is now source-qualified {"op":"col","name":"Quantity pieces","source":"stock"} instead of resolving against the root 'products' frame, which produced null for all 12 records.
Added /product_name from Master 'Description' (12 distinct, no nulls, one label per SKU).
Record dedupe keys set to /sku; quality rules: /sku not_null + unique, /qty range min 0 (warning only, so a missing stock row stays null rather than failing).

attributes_passthrough=false: the target schema declares additionalProperties:false with only sku/product_name/qty; Master's Company and Item code stay available as join keys but are not emitted (no target pointer exists for them).
No business clarification is needed: units are stated in the header ('pieces'), and there are no price, currency or VAT fields in either sheet or in the contract.
